C0300.d: C0300 appears in none of the published J2012 lists, and no maker documents it as an ABS valve code. GM uses the number: it is among the chassis keywords of PIP5094, and AA1Car's GM table calls it Rear Speed Sensor Malfunction, listed in the same block as the transfer case motor codes C0306 to C0315.
s: ABS and stability control warning lamps on
Car pulls during hard braking
c: Inlet valve sticking from contaminated or aged brake fluid
Valve coil or driver in the brake module faulty
On GM 4WD trucks, rear speed sensor fault in the transfer case system (GM meaning of the number)

C0301.d: No reachable J2012 table, no GM keyword list such as PIP5094, no AA1Car chart and no NHTSA bulletin carries C0301. Makers that document this fault use their own numbers.
s: Air suspension warning message, compressor silent
Vehicle sinks or leans after standing
Compressor runs continuously when the relay sticks
c: Relay contacts burnt or welded by excessive compressor current
Worn, seized or water-damaged compressor drawing too much current
Blown compressor fuse or corroded relay socket and wiring

C0302.d: C0302 has no public footprint: the publicly available J2012 tables, GM's PIP5094, the AA1Car chart and the NHTSA bulletin index all lack it. This text therefore covers only the front left outlet valve named in the title.
s: ABS warning lamp on, ABS switched off
Front left wheel locks or pedal sinks slowly
c: Outlet valve seat leaking because of dirt or wear
Valve coil or its driver in the brake module faulty
Old or wrong brake fluid slowing the valve

C0303.d: C0303 has no public evidence at all: the accessible J2012 lists, GM's PIP5094 keyword list, AA1Car's GM table and the NHTSA index all lack it. The title points to the front right inlet valve.
s: ABS, traction and stability control lamps on
Car pulls to the left when braking
c: Inlet valve stuck from debris after brake work
Open or shorted valve coil inside the hydraulic unit
Low supply voltage to the valve circuit during self-test

C0304.d: No public source confirms C0304; searches of the J2012 tables at hand, of GM's keyword bulletin PIP5094, of AA1Car and of the NHTSA bulletin index came up empty. The title concerns the front right outlet valve, the part that bleeds pressure off that caliper when the wheel starts to lock.
s: ABS and stability control warning lamps on
Long brake pedal or front right wheel locking
c: Outlet valve not resealing because of dirt in the seat
Valve coil or brake module output stage defective
Accumulator or return pump unable to take the released fluid

C0305.d: C0305 is missing from the published J2012 lists and is not described by any maker as an ABS valve code. GM does use it: PIP5094 lists the number, and AA1Car's GM table calls it Front Speed Sensor Malfunction, the partner of C0300 in the block before the transfer case motor codes.
s: ABS and brake warning lamps on
Rear wheel locking early or hill start assist unavailable
c: Rear left inlet valve sticking from contaminated fluid
Valve coil or brake module driver defective
On GM 4WD trucks, front speed sensor fault in the transfer case system (GM meaning of the number)

C0306.d: C0306 is not in the publicly available J2012 lists, and nobody uses it for a ride height sensor. GM uses it in its transfer case module (TCCM) for the two circuits that drive the shift motor: AA1Car's GM table names it Motor A or B Circuit, and bulletins PIP5080 and PIP5080B for 2012–13 Silverado, Sierra, Tahoe, Suburban, Avalanche and Yukon point to terminals at X109 and to connector X3 of the module, which carries
s: Service 4WD message in the driver information centre
Transfer case does not shift between 2WD, 4WD and low range
c: Loose, corroded or poorly crimped terminals at the motor or module connector
Transfer case shift motor with internal short or open winding
Faulty motor driver in the transfer case control module

C0307.d: C0307 has no public trace: not in the accessible J2012 lists, not in GM's PIP5094 or AA1Car's GM table, and not in the NHTSA bulletin index. Described here is the rear right inlet valve of the title.
s: ABS and stability control lamps on
Stability control unavailable
c: Rear right inlet valve slowed by dirt or aged fluid
Coil of the valve or brake module output defective
Poor contact between brake module and valve block

C0308.d: None of the publicly available J2012 lists contains C0308, and no source links it to a ride height sensor. GM uses it for the transfer case shift motor: PIP5094 lists the number, AA1Car's GM chart labels it Motor A/B Circuit Low, and Dorman's guide for its replacement motor covers 1998–2005 S10 Blazer, Sonoma, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon, Silverado, Sierra, Escalade, Avalanche and related trucks.
s: Service 4WD lamp on
No shifting into or out of four-wheel drive
c: Motor control wire A or B chafed against the frame and grounded
Transfer case control module output stage faulty

C0309.d: C0309 is no part of any public J2012 table, and no manufacturer documents it as a valve code. GM does use it: it is among the keywords of PIP5094, and the GM code chart on AA1Car calls it Motor A/B Circuit High, a transfer case shift motor fault next to C0308 and C0310; that meaning rests on this single source.
s: ABS and stability control warning lamps on
Weak braking at the right rear wheel
c: Rear right outlet valve not closing fully
Valve coil or brake module driver faulty
On GM 4WD trucks, transfer case motor circuit shorted to voltage (GM meaning of the number)

C0310.d: C0310 is not listed in any publicly available J2012 table; no maker uses it for a rear left ride height sensor. GM assigns the number to the transfer case shift motor: it is in PIP5094, AA1Car gives the GM wording Motor A/B Circuit Open, and Dorman describes it for GM trucks and SUVs of 1998 to 2005.
s: Service 4WD lamp on, 4WD switch lights flash
Transfer case stays in its last range
c: Broken motor control wire or pigtail exposed under the vehicle
Corroded or unseated connector at the shift motor
Open winding or worn brushes in the shift motor

C0312.d: Searches for C0312 in reachable J2012 lists, in GM sources and in the NHTSA bulletin index returned nothing, so only the component is described here. A ride height sensor at the right rear converts the swing of a lever arm linked to the suspension into an electrical signal, usually by inductive or Hall measurement, and feeds air suspension, damping or headlamp levelling.
s: Air suspension or levelling warning message
Rear right corner sits too high or too low
Headlamp levelling incorrect
c: Bent, detached or wrongly clipped sensor lever or link rod
Corroded connector or broken wire at the rear right sensor
Sensor failed internally after water ingress

C0317.d: C0317 is publicly undocumented: it is missing from every publicly available J2012 list, from GM's keyword bulletin PIP5094 and from the whole NHTSA bulletin index. What follows describes only the part named in the title.
s: Suspension warning or air suspension fault message
Vehicle sits low and does not rise
Compressor runs constantly or never starts
c: Relay contacts burnt or welded by a compressor drawing too much current
Open or shorted control line between suspension module and relay coil
Worn or seized compressor overloading the relay
Blown compressor fuse or corroded relay socket

C0327.d: C0327 has no entry in the published J2012 tables, but GM documents it: the transfer case control module (TCCM) of 4WD trucks and SUVs uses it for the encoder that tells the module where the motor has turned the shift shaft. Dorman's instruction sheets for GM pickups and SUVs from 1998 to 2009, the Saab 9-7X included, describe it as a voltage outside the expected window on the encoder circuit; play in a worn shift sha
s: Service 4WD message or flashing 4WD switch lamps
Transfer case does not shift or shifts only intermittently
Fault appears mainly on the first drive after cold or damp standing
c: Loose or corroded ground terminal for the encoder channels (GM circuit 550)
Damaged encoder harness or water in the motor connector
Encoder in the shift motor assembly defective
Worn shift shaft lets the encoder read a false position

C0374.d: No publicly available J2012 list carries C0374; GM uses it in the transfer case control module of its 4WD trucks and SUVs, and PIP5094 names it among GM chassis codes. Dorman's sheets for the S10, Blazer, Astro and Safari, the Trailblazer, Envoy and Isuzu Ascender call it General 4WD Failure: in Auto 4WD the module notices rear wheel slip, commands torque to the front axle and still sees the front and rear propshafts
s: Service 4WD message until the next engine start
Auto 4WD does not engage, rear wheels spin on slippery ground
c: Encoder motor too weak or sticking, so the clutch is not applied
Front or rear propshaft speed sensor or its wiring giving false values
Worn transfer case clutch pack or wrong fluid
Tires of unequal size or pressure faking a speed difference

C0376.d: C0376 is not in the published J2012 lists. The number exists at GM, whose bulletin PIP5094 lists it next to transfer case codes such as C0374 and C0387, but no reachable GM document states what it means.
s: Service 4WD message or flashing 4WD indicator
Front wheels not driven although 4WD is selected
Grinding or clicking from the front axle when shifting
c: Water or corrosion in the axle actuator connector
Chafed actuator harness near the axle
Disconnect actuator or its position switch defective

C0387.d: C0387 is absent from the publicly available J2012 lists. GM uses it in its transfer case control module as Unable to Complete Shift; there is no evidence of a position sensor code.
s: Service 4WD message, often intermittent
Requested range or mode is not reached
Transfer case stays in a default 4HI or 4LO
c: Encoder motor too slow to start moving the shift shaft
Poor terminal fit at the module connectors (GM X109, X3)
Low supply voltage or extreme temperatures during the shift
Mechanical binding inside the transfer case shift mechanism

C0388.d: No public source can be found for C0388; neither the reachable J2012 tables nor GM's PIP5094 or NHTSA's index of bulletins contain it. The text therefore covers only the title part.
s: Service 4WD or 4x4 warning displayed
Range indicator does not match the selected gear
Shifts out of high range refused
c: Open, shorted or corroded wire or terminal of the range switch
Range switch or position sensor on the transfer case defective
Transfer case module calibration needing an update

C0389.d: There is no evidence that any maker uses C0389. Neither the publicly available J2012 tables nor GM's chassis keyword bulletin PIP5094 nor NHTSA's index name it, so only the switch named in the title is described.
s: 4LO cannot be selected or left
4WD warning and low range indicator flashing
Stability control behaves unexpectedly after restart
c: Damaged or corroded wiring of the low range switch
Low range switch or range sensor defective
Transfer case stuck between ranges so no switch position is reached

C0399.d: C0399 cannot be traced publicly. Publicly available J2012 tables do not list it, PIP5094 from GM omits it, and the only matches in NHTSA's index are Mack recall numbers.
s: Service 4WD message
Mode changes ignored or 4WD indicators flash
c: Switch variant not matching the transfer case (e.g. Auto position without Auto 4WD)
Worn switch contacts or resistor ladder giving invalid voltages
Open or shorted lead between switch and transfer case module
